senses.sense_definition: A person who works only for money, often lacking loyalty or genuine interest in their duties.

examples.text: The company hired <w>mercenaries</w> to handle the project, but they lacked any real commitment to our goals.
She felt like a <w>mercenary</w> because she only cared about the paycheck rather than the quality of her work.

senses.sense_definition: A professional soldier hired to fight for a foreign army or group, primarily for financial reward.

examples.text: The small nation relied on <w>mercenaries</w> to defend its borders during the long and difficult war.
Many <w>mercenaries</w> were recruited from abroad to join the ranks of the rebel forces.

senses.sense_definition: A person hired to perform a difficult or aggressive task in a professional or political context.

examples.text: The firm brought in a legal <w>mercenary</w> to ensure they won the high-stakes corporate lawsuit.
He acted as a political <w>mercenary</w>, switching sides whenever a better offer came along.

senses.sense_definition: Driven primarily by the desire for money or personal advantage.

examples.text: His <w>mercenary</w> attitude toward his friends made everyone feel uncomfortable and used.
She made a <w>mercenary</w> decision to marry him solely for his vast family fortune.
